Rub-a-Dub Blues: New Album Arrives 20 November

Team Gringo's26 October 2026Album ReleasePress

Recorded live to tape in an abandoned cork factory, the third album from Gringo's Washboard Band brings twelve songs of hokum, ragtime and hot swing — and a European tour to go with it.

LISBON — 26 October 2026 — Gringo's Washboard Band today announces Rub-a-Dub Blues, its third studio album, out 20 November on Tábua Records. Produced by the band and engineered by longtime collaborator Paulo Fita, the record was made in four days with two vintage ribbon microphones, no headphones and no overdubs.

The album features eight new originals and four reworked standards from the jug band and hokum songbook. The first single, "Scrub Me Mama", is out now on all streaming platforms, with a video shot in a working laundromat in Lisbon's Arroios neighbourhood.

Listen now
Gringo's Washboard Band — Scrub Me Mama (Official Video)

The band describes it as their most honest record yet. "Everything you hear happened in the room at the same time," says washboard player Zé "Gringo" Tábuas. "If somebody laughed, it's on the record. If the bass fell over, it's on the record."

"We wanted it to sound like the best Saturday night of your life — slightly out of tune, very loud and over far too soon."— Zé "Gringo" Tábuas, washboard & vocals
"I grew up listening to my grandfather's 78s. This is the first time I feel we've come close to that sound."— Rita Banjo, banjo & vocals
"The washtub bass is now officially held together with tape and love."— Nuno Tina, washtub bass

To celebrate the release, the band heads out on the Rub-a-Dub Tour 2026, with twelve dates across Portugal, Spain, France, the Netherlands and the UK, ending with a New Year's swing cruise from Lisbon to Funchal. Tickets are on sale now.

About Gringo's Washboard Band

Formed on a Lisbon street corner in 2016, Gringo's Washboard Band is a quintet of washboard, banjo, guitar, washtub bass, kazoo and harmonica. Inspired by the jug bands of Memphis, the hokum of 1920s Chicago and Parisian hot swing, they have played hundreds of shows across Europe and are known for fully acoustic, high-energy performances that turn any room into a dance floor.
